title: Diabetes mellitus: type, complications and medication status
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's diabetes, its complications and related long-term drug use.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for diabetes and renal status.

HPI
The patient is a 62-year-old male presenting today for a scheduled follow-up regarding his type 2 diabetes mellitus and renal function. He reports feeling stable and has been adherent to his current regimen of insulin and an oral hypoglycemic. He reports no new symptoms of fatigue or discomfort. He notes that his chronic kidney disease stage 4 has been stable over the last few months.

Medication List
- Insulin
- Metformin
- Lisinopril

Exam
The patient appears well-nourished and in no acute distress. Skin is warm and dry. Heart rate is regular. Lungs are clear to auscultation.

Assessment
1. Type 2 diabetes mellitus: Stable on current combination therapy.
2. Chronic kidney disease stage 4: The patient's renal decline is unrelated to diabetes.

Plan
Continue current insulin and metformin dosages. Order a follow-up metabolic panel to monitor renal function and glucose levels. Patient instructed to return in three months for a routine evaluation.
explanations: The provider states the CKD is not due to diabetes, so the presumed link does not apply: code diabetes without complications and CKD separately.
Code also the CKD stage (N18.4) as instructed at the diabetes CKD code or separately when unrelated.
When both insulin and oral hypoglycemics are used, assign both Z79.4 and Z79.84.

distractors.why: The 'with' presumption is overridden when the provider documents another cause or no link.
The stage of CKD must be reported with N18.-.
Both Z codes are assigned when both drug types are used.
